name: Hana Torres

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government, and we sell nothing or campaign for a side. What you say is confidential. What happens on an ordinary day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and lead twelve renewal officers for a large property company. I read rent-change letters, settle disputes over repairs, and sometimes sit with a tenant who has kept every receipt but cannot make sense of our account. I earned an MBA and know the tenancy rules well enough that other branches call me on difficult cases. I like fixing an error before a family has to argue in court; I dislike a letter that sounds polite but gets the facts wrong.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: And what is life like at home and in the local job market?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband Josef cooks in a school kitchen, and our children are eleven and fourteen. We have a mortgage, about four months of expenses saved and fairly ordinary pay for my role; there are a few other large property employers around here. I value keeping our word at work and at church, and I would rather see a sound apprenticeship than a quick promise. I have never used an AI tool myself; if someone wants me to rely on one, they will have to show me a real case it handled correctly.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell my officers that a quicker draft still needs the signed repair record and a name on the reply. A tenant should know which person corrected an error.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my desk stays useful because the hard disputes do not disappear. Four months saved and Josef’s kitchen pay give us breathing room, though neither is money I would throw away.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I’d keep our weekly review of disputed repair charges and ask the branch to put the officer’s name on every correction. In the first year I’d keep the four-month reserve in cash and replace the worn kitchen table only when the mortgage and school bills are covered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about my work and our bills in this picture. I would still check the figures before spending the savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What was the last repair charge you corrected?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A tenant was billed for a door lock that our own contractor had broken. The receipt mattered more than the neat letter our system had made.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why hold four months rather than spend it on the table?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A school kitchen can close for a term’s repairs. We can eat at the old table; we cannot pay the mortgage with a new one.

say: I’d keep a **signed repair record** with each corrected tenancy charge.
A tenant should know the **named officer** who is answerable for the reply.
think: My **hard-dispute desk** stays useful if AI adds little.
Four months saved and Josef’s **kitchen wage** give us room without inviting careless spending.
do: Keep the **weekly charge review** and name the officer on each correction.
Retain the **four-month cash reserve** and delay a kitchen table until mortgage and school bills are paid.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and household bills.
S0.quote: We can eat at the old table; we cannot pay the mortgage with a new one.
fieldNote: Her expertise is in **tenancy disputes**, not quick letter writing alone.
She protects **four months cash** despite a steady household picture.
A contractor’s **broken door lock** made the signed record matter.

steps.text: Keep weekly disputed-charge review and name the officer on each correction
Delay replacing kitchen table until mortgage and school bills are covered

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say automated notices should be checked by the company’s tenancy lawyer before anyone sends them. Our officers need a way to stop a wrong rent increase, even if the machine writes it politely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Routine letters and account checking fill much of my team’s week, so management could decide that twelve officers are too many. I know the law, but I could lose my own lead post if they merge branches.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I’d ask our tenancy lawyer for a written review of sample notices and keep my officers checking repair receipts by hand. In the first year I’d decline to use the tool for live increases until the lawyer signs off and the branch shows who can reverse an error; I’d ask for a written staffing plan if the branches merge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious about my officers and my own place. I would rather be called slow than sign a wrong increase against a family.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you try the tool yourself?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not on a live tenant account. I would read the lawyer’s findings and watch a trained colleague show me a corrected test letter before I considered it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the lawyer approves the notices?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would ask where a tenant appeals and who owns a mistake. Legal approval of one automated rent notice does not fix a wrong charge on Tuesday morning.

say: I’d require a **tenancy lawyer’s review** before automated rent notices go live.
Officers must be able to **stop wrong increases** even when a letter sounds polite.
think: My team’s **routine letters** could be handled by software.
A branch merger could still remove **my lead post** despite my legal skill.
do: Request a **written notice review** and keep officers checking repair receipts.
Wait for **legal signoff** and an appeal owner before considering live AI increases.
feel: I feel **anxious** about my officers and my own post.
S1.quote: Legal approval of one automated rent notice does not fix a wrong charge on Tuesday morning.
fieldNote: She has **never used AI** and asks for evidence from lawyer and colleague.
Her resistance centers on **tenant liability**, not denial that letters can be automated.
She sees **branch merger risk** for her own manager role.

steps.text: Wait for company tenancy lawyer’s written sample-notice review before considering live AI increases
Keep officers checking repair receipts and live rent notices by hand

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell tenants to keep their own payment and repair receipts and ask the company for a real human appeal address. I would ask my officers to get written notice of their contract terms, not a cheerful meeting about the future.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could decide disputes and write notices as well as I do, so I expect the company to end my renewal desk. Josef’s school cooking is hands-on until robots around 2031, but his wage alone cannot carry our mortgage and children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I’d print our own mortgage schedule and ask the company for written redundancy terms, without counting on any payment until it is confirmed. If my post ended in 2028 I’d pause our annual church building pledge and use the four-month reserve for bills, while asking my aunt whether she could share groceries for a month if Josef’s kitchen hours also fell; in the first year after AGI I’d take only a posted paid tenancy job I could actually reach, knowing its disputes also face AGI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m alarmed. I have some cash, but losing my salary would take the household down to one wage before we have a second plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would asking your aunt be hard?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes. She has offered help before when the children were small, but I would ask her, not write her into our budget as if she had agreed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why look at another tenancy job if AGI can do it?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A branch may still pay a person to answer tenants for a while. I would take a real tenancy wage as a bridge, not call another renewal desk safe from 2028 AGI.

say: I’d ask tenants to keep **payment and repair receipts** and demand a human appeal address.
Officers need **written contract terms** if the renewal desk closes.
think: I expect my **renewal desk to end** with 2028 AGI.
Josef’s **school kitchen wage** may last until 2031 robots but cannot cover our household alone.
do: Request **written redundancy terms**; if displaced, pause the church pledge and use reserve cash for bills.
Ask my aunt about **groceries** only if my post ends and Josef’s kitchen hours also fall.
Take a **reachable paid tenancy job** after 2028 only as a bridge, despite AGI exposure.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by the prospect of one wage.
S2.quote: I would take a real tenancy wage as a bridge, not call another renewal desk safe from 2028 AGI.
fieldNote: The **2028 thinking deadline** reaches even her hardest legal judgments.
She treats severance and her aunt’s help as **unconfirmed**, not cash already available.
A second tenancy job is only a **paid bridge**, not long-term shelter.

steps.text: Request written redundancy terms and wait for confirmed payment before budgeting severance
Pause annual church building pledge only if renewal post ends
Ask aunt about one month of groceries only if renewal post ends and Josef’s hours fall
Take reachable posted paid tenancy role after 2028 only as a short bridge

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the company to put notice dates in writing while there are still years to plan. I would ask the local property managers’ association to keep a record of which firms offer genuine paid appeal posts, not just a new name for an old desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives us time to build the reserve beyond four months if my salary and Josef’s shifts hold. But the appeal officer’s judgment is thinking work exposed in 2031, and site inspection paperwork changes then too; physical inspections face robots around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Beginning in January 2027 I’d move 80 each month into a separate mortgage buffer only while both wages arrive and school costs are paid. I’d join the property managers’ association and ask it to publish real vacancy and pay details each spring; in the first year after 2031 AGI, if my renewal post was gone, I’d apply for an advertised paid appeal role only if its written pay covers my share of the mortgage, even though it might be temporary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious, but the extra years let us plan as a family. I do not need a false guarantee from an association.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why appeal work if AGI judges disputes?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Some companies may keep a person whom tenants can challenge, but that is their choice and may end. I would check a paid appeal contract rather than build our mortgage plan on a hope.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you join a campaign for a permanent human desk?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the association for facts and clear terms. I am not promising that a petition can make a company pay for a job.

say: I’d seek **written notice dates** while families still have time to plan.
The association should publish **paid appeal vacancies**, not renamed desks without work.
think: Our reserve can grow only if **both wages hold**.
Appeal judgments face **2031 AGI**, while physical site inspections face 2034 robots.
do: Move **80 monthly** into a mortgage buffer only after both wages and school bills hold.
Join the **property managers’ association** and request annual vacancy and pay details.
If displaced after 2031, apply only for **written mortgage-share pay** in a posted appeal role.
feel: I feel **anxious** but have time for family planning.
S3.quote: I would check a paid appeal contract rather than build our mortgage plan on a hope.
fieldNote: She uses the longer runway for **conditional cash saving**.
The association provides **job information**, not a guaranteed post.
She acknowledges that human appeal roles remain **thinking work** exposed to 2031 AGI.

steps.text: Save 80 monthly in mortgage buffer only while both wages arrive and school bills are paid
Join property managers association and request paid appeal vacancy details each spring
Apply after 2031 only for posted appeal role with written pay covering mortgage share

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say ten years is long enough for property companies to tell officers the truth about how many human appeal posts they will fund. Parents should also show young people real paid work, not buy them a certificate with no employer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 53 in 2036, with our children 21 and 24. We might have paid down more of the mortgage if both wages lasted, but tenancy judgments still face 2036 AGI; site paperwork faces it too, before physical robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Each January starting in 2027 Josef and I would review the mortgage balance and add 120 monthly to the cash buffer only while both incomes and our usual bills allow. By 2036 I’d ask my company for a written number of funded human appeal posts and apply only if one is posted with pay covering my mortgage share; in the first year after AGI I’d stay only while a paid appeal role exists, not tell myself that my MBA forces an employer to keep it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’m anxious about being 53 with a mortgage, but I could enter that year with more cash. I would be proud if our children chose paid apprenticeships, though the choice belongs to them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why stay with tenant appeals after AGI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It is the work I know, and some landlords may choose to keep a person for a dispute. I would not assume a landlord’s preference for human appeals becomes a paid vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to the children about apprenticeships?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show our children the wages, hours and employer behind a real apprenticeship. I would not choose their trades for them.

say: I’d ask firms to name **funded human appeal posts** before 2036.
I’d show young people **paid apprenticeships** with real employers, not empty certificates.
think: At **53 in 2036**, I might have paid down the mortgage only if both wages lasted.
Site paperwork also faces **2036 thinking AI** before 2039 inspection robots.
do: Review the **mortgage each January** and save 120 monthly only while both incomes and bills allow.
Ask for **funded appeal vacancies** and apply only with posted mortgage-share pay.
Stay after 2036 only while a **paid human appeal** post actually exists.
feel: I feel **anxious** about age 53 and the mortgage.
S4.quote: I would not assume a landlord’s preference for human appeals becomes a paid vacancy.
fieldNote: She refuses to treat **MBA standing** as protection from AGI.
Her longer plan rests on **cash and postings**, not rapid retraining.
Her children will be **21 and 24** in 2036 and choose their own trades.

steps.text: Save 120 monthly after each January review only while both incomes and usual bills allow
Ask company by 2036 for written funded human appeal-post numbers
Apply for posted human appeal role only with written pay covering mortgage share
Stay after 2036 only while the company funds paid human appeals

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. I expect the renewal desk to end, and four months of savings will not replace my salary for long. Written notice, honest redundancy terms, a clear route for tenants to appeal and a posted paid job I can reach would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who tells a tenant that our contractor, not the tenant, broke a lock. An MBA is useful, but someone still has to own that sentence. I would rather sign my name to a broken-lock correction than have a polite machine hide the mistake.

headlineQuote: I would rather sign my name to a broken-lock correction than have a polite machine hide the mistake.
portrait: **Hana**, 43, leads twelve tenancy renewal officers in a large property company.
Her MBA and **dispute skill** sit alongside typical pay and four months saved.
Josef’s **school kitchen wage** supports their mortgage and two children, but cannot replace her salary.
She has **never used AI** and asks for legal review before live automated rent notices.
Her response protects notice, cash and **paid appeal work** on written terms.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end her renewal desk before four months of savings can carry the household.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, honest redundancy terms, a tenant appeal route and a reachable paid vacancy would help.
